blocks.title: Generative Design Variations, Epilogue
blocks.description: The last publication in the Generative Design Variations series is an epilogue. Divided into four parts. First I will give a brief summary of the Generative Design Variations project. Then I have a discussion with Erik van Blokland. And two stories from the most loyal followers of the project: Jeanne de Bont and Albert Kiefer.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 10, Articles
blocks.description: This is the last publication (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed. This publication is about loading Wikipedia articles from the internet. A force-directed layout is used to create the visualizations.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 9, Hierarchy
blocks.description: This is publication nine (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed. This publication is about hierarchical structured information using the tree structure as a graphical model. The classical representation resembles an upside down tree-structure. Directories and files are good examples of tree structures.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 8, Nodes
blocks.description: This is publication eight (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed. The node is the basic starting point of all graphics in this publication. A node is a point, knot or intersection. The term is most common in mathematics, computer science and engineering.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 7
blocks.description: This is the seventh publication (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed. My first contact with 3D software was in 1994 when the commercial version of Bryce 1.0, appeared for the Apple Macintosh.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 6, Waves
blocks.description: The sixth chapter (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed is about graphics generated by waves. There are two types of waves. Mechanical and electromagnetic waves. Mechanical waves we can see at the ocean's shore or as ripples in a fountain. We can also hear them as sound.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 5, Complexity
blocks.description: The fifth chapter (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed is about complex graphics generated by randomness and noise. There are plenty books that teach you how to program. However, in this publication there is not one line of code.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 4, Photos
blocks.description: The fourth chapter (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed is about photography and video. Knowing that this chapter is about manipulating and modifying photos and movies. There are plenty books that teach you how to program. However, in this publication there is not one line of code.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 3, Fonts
blocks.description: The third chapter (of ten) that Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed is about fonts. We are not completely new in the font-world but according to Jan Middendorp in his book 'dutch type' we are the least known typographic pioneers of the Netherlands. Which is fine.

blocks.title: Generative Design Variations 2, Geometry
blocks.description: Geometry, Discovering programmed design, Henk Lamers. Jeanne de Bont and I have written and designed the second chapter of my Generative Design Variations project. This second chapter (of ten) is about geometry. There are plenty of books that teach you how to program. However, in this publication there is not one line of code.
